provenance.finalKey: cuet-2026-final-keys.pdf (NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key), subject 319, 24 shifts (23 x 85 rows, 30-05-2026 First 84 rows); rows extracted to tmp/1123-papers/mathematics/work/keys-mathematics.json

structure: Group 'Core Mathematics and Applied Mathematics' (group marks 250, 60 minutes): Section A Common, mandatory, 15 questions (306-320, 75 marks); Section B1: Mathematics, optional, 35 questions (321-355, 175 marks); Section B2: Applied Mathematics, optional, 35 questions (356-390, 175 marks). A candidate answers Section A plus one of B1 or B2 (50 questions). All 85 printed questions are in the shift's final key. Each question is printed in English, then in Hindi (same question id and option ids).
authentication: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 319 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed option ids are consecutive per question (2268953069709 to 2268953070048 across the 85 questions).
notes: Each question is printed in English, then Hindi; only the English is transcribed, read from the page images. Spelling and wording kept as printed (e.g. Q361 'payble', Q376 'a office', Q375 'characterstic', Q388 'The speed of of the stream', Q389 'will the tank is full', Q355 'envelop', Q362 'a person drive').

Math is written in plain Unicode: fractions as a/b, powers with ^ or superscripts, matrices row by row as [a b; c d], determinants as | ... ; ... |, vectors with an arrow (a⃗) and unit vectors î, ĵ, k̂.
Page = the PDF page (pNN of the 76-page PDF; the printed footer is one lower) where the question's English option ids end.
Match tables are written as rows 'List-I item | List-II item' in the order the paper prints them.
Q339 and Q351 carry figures; each is described in words inside the stem in square brackets.
Q342: the stem prints 'dy/dx + py = Q' with a small p but then says 'where P and Q are functions of x'; kept as printed. NTA's key is option 2 (y e^(∫p dx) = ∫(Q e^(∫p dx)) dx + c), the NCERT form.

Q370: NTA's key is option 4 ('decreasing function for x ∈ ℝ − {0}'). f′(x) = −2/x² < 0 on each of (−∞, 0) and (0, ∞), so f is decreasing on each interval; strictly it is not decreasing on their union (f(−1) = 3 < f(1) = 7). Option 4 is the only defensible option; kept as NTA's published key and flagged for the coverage stage.
Q385: the operator in statements C and D is printed as '÷'; with that reading NTA's key (option 1, A and D only are not correct) is right.
Every key was re-derived by working the question; all 85 agree with NTA's final key (Q370 as noted).

OCR (RapidOCR) read every option id but missed 42 of the 85 bold header lines; for those the question id was read from the page image and checked against the key (the key's option id must fall in the question's printed option-id block, and the ids run consecutively 226895791572 to 226895791656 in paper order). Where OCR did read the header (43 questions) it agrees with the visual read.

The shift's key has 85 rows, all single-answer, none dropped. NTA's final key for subject 319 holds 24 shifts; this paper is the 24-05-2026 Second shift and all 85 question ids fall in that one shift.
